items.title: 68514_Horace Henderson oral history interview
items.q: the great Lucky Millinder, and I had the pleasure of doing a few things for Hal McIntyre... Lucky Millinder had a great band.

ctx.x: -- Alabama, from the same school that the McCord brothers came from, and he turned out to be a great reading trumpet player. In fact, from my band he went to the great bands, like he played with Duke Ellington for quite a spell. He played with Lucky Millinder and his great band, and we called him Shad. That was his nickname, Shad or Scad -- I believe it's Scad. But anyway, he was a little humpback guy with great shoulders. When I say humpback, I mean he could play close up, you know, pumping. When you say…

I think one time you told me a little bit about how you had met Rex Stewart. Maybe I'm thinking of somebody else, but you told me the other night about somebody that came and nobody thought he could play, and then he suddenly just boomed out, maybe --
